comment: No source is published. The three playheads are three separate eight-float vectors built from the same nine scaled knob values, each rotated to start at a different knob: A holds knobs one to eight, B holds knobs four to nine followed by one and two, and C holds knobs seven to nine followed by one to five. That is what the panel's Start A, Start B and Start C mark, and it is the three-phase reading the maker's one-line summary claims. Each output also carries a sixteen-entry table of indices, re-drawn with three-bit random numbers only on a rising edge at Rnd trig; the Mode switch, configured as All, Phase and Step at values 0, 1 and 2, selects how much of that table is re-drawn, and on All the step counters wrap at sixteen rather than at eight. The panel prints Rnd above the switch and Step, Phase and All down its left side. The six knobs that are not a Start knob all carry the same line, because the module treats them identically. Knob values are scaled 0 to 8V on Unipolar and -8V to +8V on Bipolar.
